provenance.T1: official NFL.com pages (results, schedule, game pages, standings)
provenance.T2: licensed sportsbook prices (DraftKings) published by ESPN; archived verbatim
provenance.T4: model numbers and statistics computed in this repository from T1 and T2
provenance.note: The NFL publishes no betting lines. No price here is labelled official.

limits: The graded sample is 16 games (weeks 9-10). That is small, and every significance statement is reported against it rather than glossed over.
Depth is measured as line movement between the archived open and close. It is not order-book depth, which this repository has no source for.
Player-prop markets and prop-combo correlations are not published: no official source for player-level prices was confirmed, so those cells are left blank.

staking_vs_skill.rule: A strategy's skill rank comes from out-of-sample error only. A staking run, however good, cannot change it. Where the two ranks disagree the table says so.

correlations.label: margin vs total
correlations.definition: Pearson r between the game's final margin (home - away) and its total points (home + away)
correlations.why: The parlay-critical pair: if these co-move, a side leg and a total leg cannot be priced independently.
correlations.source: data/games-2026.csv (150 official NFL.com game pages, proved by tools/verify.py)
correlations.source_tier: T4 this repository, computed from T1 results

correlations.label: home points vs away points
correlations.definition: Pearson r between the home team's score and the away team's score
correlations.why: Measures whether a game is a shootout for both teams or only one; the input to same-game sizing.
correlations.source: data/games-2026.csv (150 official NFL.com game pages, proved by tools/verify.py)
correlations.source_tier: T4 this repository, computed from T1 results

correlations.label: total vs home win
correlations.definition: Pearson r between total points and a 1/0 home-win indicator
correlations.why: A point-biserial check: does the home side win more often in high-scoring games?
correlations.source: data/games-2026.csv (150 official NFL.com game pages, proved by tools/verify.py)
correlations.source_tier: T4 this repository, computed from T1 results

correlations.label: cover vs over
correlations.definition: Pearson r between final margin and total points, the same pair expressed for a spread leg and a total leg
correlations.why: The same-sample statement of margin-vs-total, reported separately because a parlay needs the leg-level view.
correlations.source: data/games-2026.csv (150 official NFL.com game pages, proved by tools/verify.py)
correlations.source_tier: T4 this repository, computed from T1 results

correlations.label: opening spread vs closing total
correlations.definition: Pearson r between the home spread at the open and the game total at the close
correlations.why: Does the market move the number and the total together? If not, side and total legs are closer to independent than a same-game parlay would assume.

market_anchoring.definition: For every graded spread bet, the fair handicap and the market handicap are compared in absolute value. compression_ratio below 1 means the desk's number sits closer to zero than the board's, so the desk systematically takes the underdog side. mean_difference is the average signed edge claim.
market_anchoring.source: data/market-snapshots-2026.csv (T2 prices) and the model forecasts in this payload
market_anchoring.source_tier: T4 this repository, computed from T2 prices
market_anchoring.why_it_matters: A compressed model wins the underdog side often in a season when underdogs cover, without that being skill. It is why the staking board is reported separately from the skill board and why the demotion gate reads closing-line value rather than the record.
